**Visual Analysis:**

- **Affected plant part**: Wheat heads (spikes/ears)
- **Key observations**:
  - **Left head**: Dark brown/black discoloration at rachis nodes and spikelet bases; rotted, shrunken spikelets with blackened tissue
  - **Right head**: Complete bleaching/whitening of the entire spike — classic "tombstone" or "white head" appearance
  - The combination of partial bleaching on one head and complete bleaching on the other, along with dark brown rot at spikelet bases, is the hallmark pattern
  - Some spikelets show the characteristic water-soaked brownish rot progressing from the infection point

**Reasoning through classes:**

- **Loose Smut**: Would show black powdery spore masses replacing kernels — not seen here
- **Dwarf Bunt**: Would show bunt balls (dark teliospore masses) within spikelets — not visible
- **Stem Rust / Stripe Rust / Wheat Leaf Rust**: These affect leaves/stems with urediniospore pustules — wrong location and morphology
- **Head Scab (Fusarium Head Blight)**: Matches perfectly — partial to complete spikelet bleaching ("white heads"), dark brown/black rot at rachis nodes, shrunken spikelets. The left head shows the characteristic necrotic brown lesions at spikelet bases with the infection spreading upward, while the right head shows end-stage complete bleaching.
